statement: For flat finitely presented X/S with geometrically connected fibers, a section (or the stated finite radicial substitute), and the tentative locally noetherian base condition, the author proposes a relative representation equivalence. In the broader version a strict pro-étale group Π/S and pro-Π_X torsor P have fiberwise quotient maps from the enlarged fundamental groups, and coherent continuous Π-representations should recover the coherent relatively étale-trivial stratified objects whose geometric fibers factor through Π_s.
computation: Ordinary descent constructs the associated stratified object from a representation. The source does not prove that the fiberwise quotient condition implies essential surjectivity over an arbitrary base. The ordinary profinite group is not substituted for the explicitly enlarged group.
fate: The opened dos Santos2007 §2.4 Proposition13 (author-version pp13–14) gives a point-base finite-monodromy comparison under regularity and algebraic closedness. Lara2019 Theorem3.1 (printed p7) gives a related homotopy theorem for flat proper finitely presented maps with reduced connected geometric fibers over a connected Nagata base, using near exactness. Searches for relative stratified coherent representations, enlarged/pro-étale fundamental groups, and relative homotopy sequences did not locate the exact arbitrary-base fiberwise equivalence printed here. These are related theorems, not an exact match.

present_status: As of 19 November 2026: The construction direction and restricted finite-monodromy cases are established. The exact broad relative equivalence remains an identification/formulation gap in this audit; neither a proof nor a counterexample to its complete quantifiers has been established. Modern Noohi pro-étale groups must not automatically be identified with the historical enlarged pro-group.

statement: For a given stratified invertible sheaf L on finite-type geometrically unibranch X/k, the proposed criterion is étale-local triviality iff L^n is trivial as a stratified sheaf for some n>0 prime to char(k). The sufficiency direction is asserted without geometric unibranchness. Torsion of the underlying ordinary line bundle alone is only a necessary condition, not the stated iff.
computation: The forward direction in the standard smooth connected algebraically closed-field setting uses finite image of a continuous rank-one representation of a profinite group; a finite subgroup of k* has prime-to-p order. For the reverse direction, the roots of a horizontal trivialization of L^n form an étale μ_n-torsor, and its tautological root is horizontal. Over nonclosed fields, retain relative descent/group-scheme data rather than replacing it by the full arithmetic étale group.
fate: Stacks Lemma59.65.2 (tag0GIY) verifies finite Galois trivialization of finite-type locally constant module sheaves on irreducible geometrically unibranch schemes. dos Santos2007 Proposition13 supplies the regular algebraically closed positive-characteristic comparison and explicitly warns on p14 against the same formula over a nonclosed field. These open texts and the independent Kummer proof settle the usual setting and sufficiency; an exact primary proof including every singular/arbitrary-field convention of the manuscript was not located.

statement: The equivalence of étale/Zariski local pullback-triviality with curvature and p-curvature zero is false for arbitrary quasi-coherent E if localization means neighborhoods in X over the fixed base S, as the definition of triviality suggests.
computation: For S=Spec F_p and X=A1, E=O_X/(x^p) with the induced d has zero curvature and p-curvature and descends through relative Frobenius from O_Xprime/(u). It is nonzero torsion at the origin and cannot become a pullback of a vector space under an étale neighborhood. This is a written proof, not a textual comparison.
fate: Opened Katz1970 Theorem5.1, printed pp190–191, gives the precise quasi-coherent Cartier equivalence, which is weaker than local freeness. dos Santos2007 introduction independently emphasizes failure of local freeness for positive-characteristic integrable connections. The counterexample refutes the literal local-triviality implication, while the descent part survives as C-SA04-701.

statement: Under the smooth characteristic-p (or the stated local p-basis) hypothesis, relative Frobenius pullback with its canonical connection is an equivalence from quasi-coherent sheaves on Xprime to quasi-coherent integrable connections with zero p-curvature. Matching coherent categories may also be used under the usual noetherian finite-presentation assumptions; one cannot mix coherent source with all quasi-coherent target.
computation: Katz gives the horizontal-sections inverse and a local Taylor projector. A finite locally free descended module has local bases; their Frobenius pullbacks are horizontal frames. Local freeness is preserved and reflected by faithfully flat Frobenius, so the locally trivial bundle version is valid. An infinite direct sum of trivial objects also witnesses the source-category size mismatch if line320 is read literally.
fate: Exact modern formulation opened in Katz1970 Theorem5.1, printed pp190–191, with smoothness, characteristic-p base, and both categories quasi-coherent. The author attributes the result to Cartier. The printed coherent/quasi-coherent mismatch is a separate possible transcription or formulation error.

statement: The scan198 e) criterion is false even when every reduction has a lift rational over its residue field: an integral finite-type base dominating Spec Z and an abelian scheme section need not be torsion merely because all closed reductions lift through Verschiebung.
computation: Complete proof in root_supplement_proofs.md: S=Spec Z[1/30], E:y²=x³−2x, P=(2,2), discriminant512. For every p≥7 the rational two-torsion makes Np even; Hasse gives 0<Np<2p; thus p does not divide Np. VF=[p] and bijectivity of F on Fp-points give a rational V-lift for every point. Exact counts at3 and5 are4 and10, so good-reduction injectivity bounds rational torsion by2; P has y≠0 and infinite order. Saved program b_supplement_computations.py and output verify the finite calculations.
fate: Primary ingredients opened: Milne2021 II§5 Cor5.7 p66 (torsion specialization), IV§9 Thm9.4 p150 (Hasse); Chai–Oort2009 §10.24 p531 (VF=FV=p). Searches on Verschiebung-divisible reductions did not locate this exact manuscript formulation as a published theorem; the counterexample resolves the literal statement independently. This supplements/refines root C-SA04-644, not a second manuscript occurrence.

statement: Assuming the finite-monodromy rank-one criterion and that every global unit is horizontal for the canonical relative stratification, an étale-trivial stratification on O_X is the standard one. Consequently, forgetting stratification identifies étale-trivial stratified line classes with prime-to-characteristic torsion in Pic(X) in this setting; the source names proper separable X/k as an example.
computation: Choose n prime to p and a horizontal trivializing section σ of (O_X,T)^n. Write 1^n=λσ. The horizontal-unit hypothesis makes 1^n horizontal; the infinitesimal stratification ratio for1 is an nth root of unity equal to1 on the diagonal, hence1 is horizontal. Existence for any prime-to-p torsion ordinary line is supplied by its μ_n-torsor; uniqueness follows by tensoring two structures and applying the result on O_X.
fate: This is an elementary Kummer consequence of the precisely stated C-SA04-699, independently reconstructed here. Searches on finite-monodromy rank-one stratifications and the opened dos Santos finite-monodromy comparison corroborate the setting; no separate historical first appearance is established.

statement: For an integral finite-type S dominating Spec Z, smooth finite-type X/S, and a vector bundle with flat relative connection, finite-étale triviality on the generic fiber implies zero p-curvature on every positive-characteristic fiber over some open neighborhood of the generic point.
computation: Spread the finite étale trivializing cover and its horizontal trivialization to a nonempty open of S. Shrink once to retain finite étale surjectivity and the finitely presented connection identities. In each residue characteristic, the trivial connection has zero p-curvature; faithful flat descent along the cover reflects its vanishing. This proves only the forward implication.
fate: Katz1970 §5, notably Proposition5.2 and Theorem5.9, supplies the p-curvature functoriality used in the spreading/descent argument. The converse is the distinct arithmetic conjecture recorded by root C-SA04-641, whose modern status is handled there.

statement: The p-curvature target in relative dimension greater than one is End(E)⊗F*Ω¹_(Xprime/S), not the literal full tensor power End(E)⊗(Ω¹)^(⊗p). For a line, the Cartier defect must use the additive Frobenius-power map rather than the generally nonadditive ordinary tensor-power expression.
computation: In characteristic2, (dx+dy)⊗(dx+dy)−dx⊗dx−dy⊗dy=dx⊗dy+dy⊗dx≠0. The four coefficients [0,1,1,0] are checked in the saved supplement program. Thus the claimed additivity cannot hold in the ordinary tensor square. On curves Ω¹ has rank1 and the appropriate identification holds.
fate: Katz1970 Proposition5.2, printed pp191–192, proves additive p-linearity, which yields the Frobenius-pullback target by linear algebra. This locates the mathematical correction; whether the author intended Frobenius tensor notation or a symmetric Frobenius-power submodule remains a reading question.

statement: In equation(4.1), the kernel of p-curvature modulo its formal completion is the nilpotent-p-curvature locus Pcin, not the zero-p-curvature locus Pcip as printed.
computation: On A1 over F2[ε]/ε², the flat connection d+εx dx has p-curvature ε: (∂+εx)²=ε. It is nonzero but nilpotent. Therefore it lies in the displayed kernel and outside Pcip. The exact saved matrix check on basis1,x corroborates the full differential-operator proof in root_supplement_proofs.md. The following(4.2) correctly distinguishes the loci.

statement: Over a perfect field of characteristic p, for an abelian variety B, the extension 0→α_B→B^(p)→B→0 given by Verschiebung is universal among commutative extensions of B by affine commutative groups H with V_H=0, with the usual finite-type/fppf conventions.
computation: For any extension0→H→E→B→0, naturality makes V_E:E^(p)→E kill H^(p) when V_H=0. It descends to a lift u:B^(p)→E of V_B. Its restriction α_B→H gives the pushout presentation. Any two lifts differ by a map B^(p)→H, which is zero because an abelian variety has only constant maps to an affine group and a group map sends zero to zero. Thus the pushout map is unique.
fate: The precise universal formulation was searched using Verschiebung, affine Vkilled extensions, Cartier duality and universal vector extensions. Opened Chai–Oort2009 §10.24 supplies natural Verschiebung for flat commutative groups; Fonseca–Matthes2022 §2.2 supplies the neighboring vector-extension universal property and cites Mazur–Messing I.1.10. No opened primary source with this exact Vkilled-affine universal formulation was located. The above independent proof establishes the stated perfect-field finite-type interpretation; historical attribution remains unassigned.
fate_date: The manuscript layer is undated. Checked edition/publication dates do not date these sheets; no first-circulation date is inferred.
present_status: As of 19 November 2026: Mathematically proved here for the explicitly stated commutative perfect-field category. The category and general-base extension require specification before promoting the source into a broader relative theorem.

statement: Let A=B* and α_B=kerV_B. The universal vector extension of B is the pushout of its Verschiebung extension along the universal linear vector-group map α_B→V(Lie(A)^dual). The finite group whose vector envelope is used is α_B; its Cartier dual kerF_A has height one and supplies the Lie-space description.
computation: For a finite group α with Cartier dual β, primitives in O(α)=O(β)* identify with Lie(β). Hence Hom(α,Ga)=Lie(β)=Lie(A) here; more generally maps to vector groups are represented by Lie(A)^dual with linear maps between vector groups. Apply the universal pushout in C-SA04-707 to H=Ga^r (whose Verschiebung is zero). This gives the standard vector-extension universal property. A literal antecedent referring the vector envelope to β instead of α would be wrong: Hom(μ_p,Ga)=0.
fate: Opened Fonseca–Matthes2022 §2.2, pp2–3, verifies the usual universal vector extension and its Hom-to-Ext property, citing Mazur–Messing I.1.10. The α_B pushout derivation is independently supplied here, with the linearity convention explicit. The precise historical wording and antecedent are not certified from ink.

present_status: As of 19 November 2026: The corrected, carefully typed pushout statement is proved. The phrase vector envelope must use α_B and linear morphisms of vector groups; it is not a universal property for all additive-polynomial morphisms of affine groups.

statement: For smooth surjective X→S with geometrically connected fibers in characteristic zero, the author asserts full faithfulness of pullback from quasi-coherent base modules to relative connections, tentatively restricting to finitely presented modules.
computation: Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field and connected smooth X, horizontal regular functions are constant, so horizontal maps between trivial bundles are constant matrices; this proves the finite-dimensional point-base case. The arbitrary-base and quasi-coherent quantifiers require a relative constants/descent argument, not just this field calculation.
fate: Searches for relative horizontal constants, pullback full faithfulness and stratified fundamental groups led to the opened point-base dos Santos comparison and relative Lara homotopy theorem, neither of which is an exact proof of this characteristic-zero arbitrary-base quasi-coherent statement. It remains a precise bibliographic/proof-check gap in this audit, not a claim that the statement is new or false.
